blocks.text: **The problem.** You're given a node from a **circular** singly linked list whose values are sorted in non-decreasing order when read round the ring — but the node you're given can be **any** node, not necessarily the smallest. Insert `insertVal` so the ring stays sorted, and return the node you were given. If the list is empty, create a one-node ring and return it.

blocks.text: The idea: three places a value can go

Walk round the ring with two pointers, `prev` and `curr = prev.next`, looking at each **gap** between neighbours. A sorted ring has exactly one place where the values **drop** — from the largest back to the smallest. That gives three cases:

**1. Between two values:** `prev.val ≤ x ≤ curr.val` — insert here. **2. At the drop** (`prev.val > curr.val`): if `x` is a new largest (`x ≥ prev.val`) or a new smallest (`x ≤ curr.val`), it goes between the largest and the smallest — insert here. **3. All the way round** without either case: every value is the same, so any gap works. In every case, insertion is the same two pointer changes: `prev.next = node; node.next = curr`.
1. Find the smallest node first, then walk up from it

blocks.code:
def insert(head, insert_val):
    node = ListNode(insert_val)
    if head is None:
        node.next = node
        return node
    mx = head
    while mx.next is not head and mx.val <= mx.next.val:   # pass 1: the largest node
        mx = mx.next
    mn = mx.next
    prev = mx                                    # a new max or min goes between max and min
    if mn.val < insert_val < mx.val:
        prev = mn                                # pass 2: walk up from the smallest
        while prev.next.val < insert_val:
            prev = prev.next
    node.next = prev.next
    prev.next = node
    return head

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(1)** — but up to two passes. Turning the ring back into a normal sorted list (find where it starts) is the instinctive move; the next version notices you don't need to.

blocks.caption: Check each gap: between two values, at the drop, or all the way round.

blocks.code:
def insert(head, insert_val):
    node = ListNode(insert_val)
    if head is None:                     # empty: a ring of one
        node.next = node
        return node
    prev, curr = head, head.next
    while True:
        if prev.val <= insert_val <= curr.val:          # fits between two values
            break
        if prev.val > curr.val and (insert_val >= prev.val or insert_val <= curr.val):
            break                                       # at the drop: a new max or min
        prev, curr = curr, curr.next
        if prev is head:                 # all the way round: every value is equal
            break
    prev.next = node                     # insert between prev and curr
    node.next = curr
    return head

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(1)** in a single pass. The `do … while` checks the gap after the head first and stops after exactly one lap — the circular-list version of **stop when you're back where you started**.

blocks.alt: Find min, then walk: O(n) time, O(1) space. One pass, three cases: O(n) time, O(1) space.

blocks.text: Both are linear; the one-pass version is shorter and is the answer interviewers expect. The three cases — **between**, **at the drop**, **all equal** — are the part worth remembering.

items: **Empty list** — return a new node that points to itself.
**One node** — the new node and the old one point at each other.
**A new largest or smallest value** — it must go at the drop, not after the given node.
**All values equal** — no gap qualifies; the lap must end and insert anyway, instead of looping forever.
**Returning the new node instead of the given one** — the caller expects the node they passed in (unless the list was empty).
**Insert into a sorted singly linked list** — the same **between two values** check, plus a special case for the new head.
**Merge two sorted circular lists** — cut each open at its smallest node, merge, and close the result.
**Sorted circular doubly linked list** — the same cases, with four pointer changes for the insert.
